title: Fringe Show 6: Diary of a Gay Disaster ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ @Edinburgh Festival F...
transcript: Diary of a Gay Disaster is such a fun musical comedy. That's one of the few shows I saw at fringe that I need a cast recording of immediately. Diary of a Gay Disaster is a fun, Sapphic musical comedy that's all about this young lesbian who wakes up in this fever dream state, being visited by these two guardian angels armed with a magic diary to help her through some of her issues. The framing device is a bit all over the place. I'm not sure if these guardian angels are also real people, if they also have their own issues that they're working through, because they definitely also work through issues during the course of the show. But the clarity really comes from the absolutely hilarious musical numbers. Each musical number is that working through an issue. A lot of them have to deal with lesbian stereotypes and sometimes working against those stereotypes. The score is full of bops and very reminiscent of, like, an early 2 in comedy. Like thinking an early Lindsay Lohan film. Like the soundtrack to A Freaky Friday or confessions of a shopaholic. Like, those are the vibes that the songs are giving, but they're also just real, really, really funny. Like you have songs like is she Queer? Just a hipster, and everybody wants to be gay. But it's not just fun and light. There's also a lot of, like, really great nuanced conversations. Is especially surrounding the non binary character and What it means to be non binary and also identify as a lesbian. As a non binary person myself, I'm constantly looking for good non binary representation, and this show absolutely nailed it. I love love, love, love the representation in the show. Well, this is definitely a musical where I would classify the book needing work. The score is just so much fun, the representation so specific and nuanced, and the performances are absolutely fantastic. I had such a fun time seeing this show. It's currently playing at fringe at Underbelly Cowgate and it's play right after Diva Live from hell, which I also just reviewed and absolutely loved. They make a perfect companion pieces to each other. I highly recommend going seeing both. This is also a late night show playing at ten ten PM and it is just full of so much energy. It's the perfect way to end your night.
